slides.text: When Detective Clara Hayes inherited the cold-case file of heiress Eleanor Vance, she immediately returned to the abandoned Victorian manor where Eleanor had vanished twenty years prior. Forensic teams had torn through floorboards and plumbing decades ago without finding a trace of blood or forced entry. But Clara noticed something the original team had missed: the parlor fireplace was flanked by two antique brass acoustic speaking tubes that ran down into the masonry foundations of the cellar.

Clara uncapped the brass horn and brought her ear close. To her astonishment, the pipe was not silent. A faint, rhythmic scratching sound drifted up through forty feet of galvanized metal, accompanied by the muffled click of knitting needles. It was physically impossible—the house had been condemned and padlocked by court order since 2004. Clara called for her partner, grabbed a sledgehammer, and descended into the damp cellar, following the vertical shaft into an unmapped sub-basement sealed behind false stone.

Beneath the rubble lay a fully furnished, airtight chamber lit by dying battery lanterns. Inside, a skeleton in an embroidered velvet dress sat upright in an armchair, holding a pair of ivory knitting needles connected to an automated clockwork pendulum that kept them clicking against the brass pipe. On the mahogany table sat a handwritten confession dated this morning: 'Thank you for finding her, Detective Hayes. Now someone is finally here to take my place.' The heavy iron door behind Clara slammed shut.
